metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. (hamstring) placed on IR
metadata.description: The New York Giants have placed running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. on injured reserve after suffering a hamstring injury in Week 7's win.
metadata.analysis: Tracy suffered an injury during the Giants' win over the Houston Texans, a game in which he carried the ball six times for 15 yards and a score. The third-year running back had seen an uptick in snaps after playing 3% or fewer in the opening three weeks, scoring three touchdowns in the last two weeks. Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary will lead the way for a New York running back room that bounced back in Week 7. Tracy is eligible to return in Week 13, given New York's Week 8 bye.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy - Move to IR official
metadata.description: The Giants placed Tracy (hamstring) on injured reserve Tuesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Just as general manager Joe Schoen indicated would be the case earlier in the day, Tracy was deactivated after straining his hamstring during Sunday's 27-21 overtime win over the Texans. He'll be out for at least the next four games, making the Giants' Week 13 game against the 49ers his earliest possible return date. While Tracy is sidelined, Devin Singletary is expected to operate as the top complement to Cam Skattebo (hamstring), who thrived while moving back into a lead role out of the backfield in the Week 7 victory.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy - Bound for IR
metadata.description: Giants general manager Joe Schoen said Tuesday that Tracy (hamstring) is slated to be placed on injured reserve, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Per Duggan, Schoen added that the hamstring injury that Tracy sustained in Sunday's overtime win over the Texans isn't season-ending, but the running back's impending move to IR means that he won't be eligible to play in any of the Giants' next four games. With Tracy out through at least Week 12, Devin Singletary should will be in line to serve as the top complement to lead back Cam Skattebo (hamstring). The Giants are planning to sign Greg Desrosiers off the Chargers' practice squad to add depth to the position group, according to Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. Headed to Injured Reserve
metadata.description: The New York Giants are placing running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. (hamstring) on Injured Reserve after he exited the team's Week 7 overtime win over the Texans with a hamstring injury. The Giants' running back room has seen its share of intrigue over the past weeks. One week after being held without a touch as an unofficial punishment for his fumbling issues, second-year back Cam Skattebo ran for a career-high 124 yards, but also tweaked his hamstring on a 42-yard run in overtime. The Giants are on bye in Week 8, but with Tracy now slated to miss at least four games, and Skattebo facing potential limitations of his own, veteran Devin Singletary becomes a top waiver stash for fantasy managers with the luxury to take a wait-and-see approach.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy - Unable to return to Sunday's win
metadata.description: Tracy (hamstring) didn't return to Sunday's 27-21 overtime win over the Texans after exiting with 5:29 remaining in the second quarter, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports.
metadata.analysis: The Giants had listed Tracy as questionable to return to the game, and though he was able to rejoin the team on the sideline during the second half, he didn't end up checking back into the contest at any point. Before exiting the contest, Tracy carried six times for 15 yards and a touchdown and added a two-yard reception over 10 total snaps on offense. Cam Skattebo (hamstring) led the New York backfield in snaps (37), touches (18) and yards from scrimmage (121) Sunday and looks to have re-established himself as the top option heading into a Week 8 bye after being limited to just six snaps a week earlier in a loss to the Saints.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. Appears to Have Avoided Serious Hamstring Injury
metadata.description: New York Giants running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. (hamstring) does not appear to have suffered a serious injury during Sunday's 27-21 overtime victory over the Houston Texans, according to Dan Duggan of The Athletic, who described a sense of relief in the Giants' locker room with the team's bye week approaching and indicated the issue did not appear significant. The 26-year-old exited in the second quarter and did not return, finishing with six carries for 15 yards and a touchdown, along with one reception for two yards. New York's Week 8 bye gives Tracy additional recovery time before the Giants visit the Philadelphia Eagles on November 8, though his availability for that matchup remains uncertain.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. (hamstring) questionable to return
metadata.description: Giants RB Tyrone Tracy Jr. is questionable to return against Houston due to a hamstring injury.
metadata.analysis: Tracy walked off the field gingerly after his last rush and now is officially questionable to return. Cam Skattebo will see an uptick in carries if Tracy cannot return, with Devin Singletary serving as the backup.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy - Exits Sunday with hamstring issue
metadata.description: Tracy left Sunday's game at Houston due to a hamstring injury, Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Tracy made his way off the field slowly with 5:29 left in the second quarter and was deemed questionable to return not long afterward. At the time of his exit, he had six carries for 15 yards and one touchdown and one catch (on one target) for two yards. Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary will handle the Giants backfield for as long as Tracy is sidelined.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. Questionable to Return With Hamstring Injury
metadata.description: New York Giants running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. (hamstring) is questionable to return to Sunday's Week 7 matchup against the Houston Texans, according to ESPN's Jordan Raanan, and Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary would absorb additional backfield work if he cannot. Tracy scored New York's first touchdown on a two-yard run in the opening quarter before suffering the injury, and he had recorded two carries for zero yards and one reception for two yards at the time of the report. He was coming off his most productive game of the season, totaling 45 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns against the New Orleans Saints in Week 6. With Najee Harris no longer on the roster, Skattebo entered Sunday's contest looking to regain a significant role after receiving no carries in Week 6.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy - Likely to remain factor in RB rotation
metadata.description: Cam Skattebo is expected to reclaim duties as the Giants' starting running back in Sunday's game against the Texans, but Tracy is expected to remain "heavily in the mix," Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: After receiving at least 15 touches in each of the Giants' first five games, Skattebo had his playing time scaled back dramatically in the Week 6 loss to the Saints, logging no carries or receptions while playing just six snaps on offense. The main beneficiary of Skattebo's role reduction was Tracy, who carried six times for 18 yards and a touchdown while adding two receptions for 27 yards and another score across a season-high 29 offensive snaps. The Giants' decision to pare back Skattebo's workload looks to be a one-time arrangement as a result of his fumble issues in the prior five contests, and while Skattebo should take back an increased workload in Week 7, Tracy won't be phased out of the game plan entirely. Raanan speculates that the Giants will proceed with "close to a 50/50 split" between the two backs Sunday, with Devin Singletary picking up any of the remaining snaps out of the backfield.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. Draws Waiver Interest After Two-Touchdown Performance
metadata.description: New York Giants running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. is a speculative waiver addition in 12-team leagues, more attractive as a bench stash than an immediate starter because of the uncertain workload and the Giants' Week 8 bye. He has an opportunity to expand his role after head coach John Harbaugh acknowledged Friday that he has earned more carries. Tracy rushed six times for 18 yards and a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints in Week 6, adding two receptions for 27 yards and another score. The Giants subsequently released Najee Harris, leaving Tracy, Devin Singletary, and Cam Skattebo competing for backfield opportunities. Singletary played 31 offensive snaps against the Saints compared to Tracy's 29, while Skattebo was limited to six snaps without a touch, and Harbaugh also praised Skattebo's practice performance, leaving the Week 7 distribution uncertain. The Houston Texans have allowed just 3.4 yards per carry to opposing running backs, a difficult matchup for a crowded backfield.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. Making Case for More Work in Week 7
metadata.description: New York Giants running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. had his best game of the 2026 season in Week 6 and hopes to keep pushing for the starting job in New York. Tracy had six carries for 18 yards and a touchdown, and added two receptions for 27 yards and a touchdown in the 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints. After a quiet start to the season, Tracy played his largest role, with his most carries, targets, and snaps of the season. With Cam Skattebo benched last week, both Devin Singletary and Tracy led the team in usage against the Saints' weaker run defense. However, the Giants face the Houston Texans' defense, which has allowed the fewest rushing yards and the third-lowest yards per carry this season. Skattebo and Singletary are both expected to share the backfield with Tracy, and with Houston posing a difficult matchup, Tracy is not a starting option this week.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. Could Emerge as Giants' Lead Running Back
metadata.description: New York Giants running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. could see a larger workload moving forward, according to ESPN's Dan Graziano. In six games this season, Tracy has 13 carries for 40 yards and a touchdown, plus four receptions for 52 yards and a touchdown. The Giants' backfield saw a major shakeup last week, with Cam Skattebo playing just six snaps and taking no carries, despite being the team's lead back through the first five games. With Skattebo phased out and veteran Najee Harris released on Tuesday, Tracy could be in line for an increased workload in Week 7. Fantasy managers should roster Tracy in most leagues this week, as he could emerge as the lead back, assuming the Giants don't add another back at this year's trade deadline.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. Leads Giants in Touches, but Backfield Job Remains Open
metadata.description: New York Giants running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. scored twice on just eight touches in Sunday's 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints, but his production hasn't secured him the lead role in New York's crowded backfield. Tracy rushed six times for 18 yards and a five-yard touchdown while catching two passes for 27 yards, including a 17-yard score. His six carries nearly matched the seven he accumulated through the first five games combined, although Devin Singletary played more offensive snaps and Najee Harris started before managing just two yards on four attempts. Cam Skattebo, whose fumbling problems cost him the starting job, played only six snaps without a touch. Head coach John Harbaugh acknowledged afterward that none of his running backs has established himself as the clear lead option. Rostered in 4% of leagues, Tracy is worth a speculative addition in 12-team formats, but his limited workload makes him difficult to trust against Houston in Week 7. New York also has its bye in Week 8.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. finds the end zone twice Sunday
metadata.description: Tyrone Tracy Jr. ran for 18 yards and a touchdown in the Giants 34-27 loss against the Saints. He also caught 2-of-3 targsts for 27 yards receiving and another touchdown.
metadata.analysis: It was an ugly afternoon for the entire Giants backfield. Tracy will be a risky flex play at best next week against the Texans.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy - Two TDs on eight touches in loss
metadata.description: Tracy rushed six times for 18 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-27 loss to the Saints. He added two catches for 27 yards and an additional touchdown on three targets.
metadata.analysis: With Cam Skattebo seemingly benched after losing a fumble in overtime against the Commanders last Sunday, Tracy played a season-high 29 offensive snaps and led the team with six rushing attempts. Only Devin Singletary (31 snaps) played more on offense, as Najee Harris (11 snaps) got the nominal start. Skattebo was in for just six offensive plays. It's unclear if the Giants will continue to punish Skattebo next Sunday against the Texans, but this looks like a backfield to avoid in fantasy.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. Scores Twice as Giants Shift to Four-Man Backfield
metadata.description: New York Giants running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. logged six carries, 18 rushing yards, two receptions, 27 receiving yards, and two total touchdowns during Sunday's Week 6 loss against the New Orleans Saints. The Giants completely shook up their backfield this week, carrying four active running backs and drastically altering how many touches each back handled. The most seismic shift involved Cam Skattebo, who had zero carries and played less than 10% of the snaps. However, Tracy's upward trajectory is notable, too. As the Giants look for one running back to separate themselves from the rest, Tracy's two touchdowns on Sunday will help his case. Managers should consider adding Tracy off the waiver wire in Week 7, but we'd want to see a little more consistent production from the 26-year-old before committing to him in fantasy lineups on a weekly basis.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy - Recaptures third-down role
metadata.description: Tracy is expected to continue serving as the Giants' primary third-down back in Sunday's game against the Saints, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: After being plagued by fumbles in the preseason and then losing another in the season-opening win over Dallas, Tracy appeared to be getting phased out of the New York offense. He was limited to just four total offensive snaps over the Giants' first three games, but Tracy has since appeared to regain some trust as a change-of-pace option over the past two weeks. After logging double-digit snaps Week 4 against the Cardinals, Tracy played a season-high 17 snaps in the Week 5 tie with the Commanders while carrying three times for six yards and adding two receptions for 25 yards on three targets. With fellow backs Cam Skattebo (four fumbles, one lost) and Najee Harris (one lost fumble) having had their own ball-security issues so far this season, head coach John Harbaugh may be willing to open up more work for Tracy beginning with Sunday's game. Per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com, Harris is expected to supplant Skattebo as the Week 6 starter, but the Giants could look to incorporate a four-man committee that also includes Tracy and Devin Singletary.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. sees five touches in Week 5
metadata.description: Tyrone Tracy Jr. rushed three times for six yards while also catching two of his three targets for 25 yards in the Giants' 27-27 tie with the Washington Commanders in Week 5.
metadata.analysis: Tracy Jr. has underwhelmed out of the New York backfield to this point, rushing for less than 15 yards in each of the first five contests. The running back remains best left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 6 contest against the New Orleans Saints.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. logs one carry in win Sunday
metadata.description: Tyrone Tracy Jr. rushed the ball one time for -1 yards in Sunday's 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals.
metadata.analysis: The veteran running back was not very involved on Sunday, seeing just one touch on the offensive side of the ball in a win over the Cardinals. He is low in the pecking order right now and will continue to be an irrelevant fantasy option moving forward as a result.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. Cleared to Play in Week 4
metadata.description: New York Giants running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. will head into Sunday's matchup against the Arizona Cardinals injury-free after a full practice Friday. The third-year back out of Purdue was bothered by a knee issue that forced him to miss Wednesday's practice. However, he upgraded his participation each of the next two days as the team preps for the visiting Cardinals. Following a subpar preseason performance, Tracy has fallen out of favor with the Giants' coaching staff, totaling three carries for 17 yards across four snaps. He appears to be a distant fourth option behind backfield mates Najee Harris, Cam Skattebo, and Devin Singletary, and can be safely avoided by fantasy managers in all formats.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy - Set for Sunday
metadata.description: Tracy (knee) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
metadata.analysis: Tracy upgraded his practice participation level in each of the Giants' Week 4 prep sessions. The running back went from a DNP on Wednesday to limited Thursday before finally achieving full participation Friday, in time to avoid any injury designation. Tracy is set to suit up for Sunday's game as the No. 3 option behind Cam Skattebo and Najee Harris.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy - Upgrades practice participation level
metadata.description: Tracy (knee) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Tracy didn't practice at all Wednesday, so his return (albeit in a limited fashion) Thursday is a sign that he's improving. The third-year pro seems to have a chance of playing Week 4 against Arizona, though he'll likely have an injury designation heading into the weekend if he's not able to practice fully Friday. Even if Tracy does suit up Sunday, he's unlikely to have a major role on offense given that he's logged just four offensive snaps through three contests on the campaign.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. (knee) upgraded to limited Thursday
metadata.description: Tyrone Tracy Jr. (knee) was upgraded to a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Tracy was able to return to practice on Thursday and put up a limited session after being sidelined on Wednesday. He seems likely to play in Week 4 but will likely not see much work on offense even if active against the Cardinals.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. (knee) returns to practice Thursday
metadata.description: Tyrone Tracy Jr. was back at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Tracy was sidelined from practice to open the week on Wednesday. He remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy - Nursing knee injury
metadata.description: Tracy (knee) did not practice Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Head coach John Harbaugh told reporters after Wednesday's session that Tracy is considered day-to-day and believes the knee injury isn't a serious matter. Tracy has mostly played on special teams this season, but if he's not cleared to play against the Cardinals on Sunday, then Devin Singletary -- who was a healthy scratch for Week 3 against the Titans -- would serve as the Giants' RB3 behind Cam Skattebo and Najee Harris.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. (knee) a non-participant Wednesday
metadata.description: Tyrone Tracy Jr. (knee) was a non-participant at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: A knee injury left Tracy sidelined at practice on Wednesday. It's still early in the week, so if he returns to practice on Thursday, fantasy managers should expect him to play and see his usual minimal workload in Week 4.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. uninvolved in win Sunday
metadata.description: Tyrone Tracy Jr. rushed the ball just one time for three yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.
metadata.analysis: It looks like the veteran has been nearly entirely phased out of this offense. He saw just one opportunity on Sunday and was completely outmatched by Najee Harris, who himself saw nine. Tracy won't be a relevant name in this backfield for the foreseeable future.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy - Loses spot in backfield rotation
metadata.description: Tracy played only one offensive snap during the Giants' 28-6 loss to the Rams on Monday.
metadata.analysis: Tracy's lone offensive play -- a carry on which he lost three yards in the fourth quarter -- didn't end up counting due to a penalty. The third-year running back did play 16 snaps on special teams and returned two kickoffs for 52 yards. That appears to be Tracy's path to playing time at the moment, as he is firmly behind Cam Skattebo, Devin Singletary and Najee Harris in the backfield pecking order.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. held without a touch Monday
metadata.description: Tyrone Tracy Jr. did not see a single carry or target in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
metadata.analysis: New York seems to have phased Tracy out of the offense altogether, as he was relegated to just special teams against the Rams and saw no opportunities on offense. Najee Harris worked in and saw four touches on the night, so it looks like the 26-year old may have lost his spot as a depth piece in the backfield.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy - Healthy ahead of Week 2
metadata.description: Tracy (illness) did not appear on the Giants' injury report Thursday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Tracy was dealing with an illness to open the week, but he now appears to be back to full health. The running back logged just two snaps with the offense Week 1 against the Cowboys, losing a fumble on his second and final carry of the contest. Tracy figures to once again operate as the No. 3 option in the backfield behind starter Cam Skattebo and top backup Devin Singletary during Monday night's contest against the Rams.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. Off Giants Injury Report on Thursday
metadata.description: New York Giants running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. (illness) is not listed on his team's Thursday injury report, per Dan Salomone of Giants.com. Tracy Jr. missed practice on Wednesday due to an illness. The 26-year-old's 2026 season got off to a rough start in Week 1, as he recorded just two carries and lost a fumble in his team's win over the Dallas Cowboys. Entering Week 2, Tracy Jr. appears to be behind not only Giants RB1 Cam Skattebo but also veteran back Devin Singletary on the team's running back depth chart. The Giants also have another veteran back on their roster in Najee Harris, who could eventually pass Tracy Jr. on the depth chart as well. Barring a change of scenery or multiple injuries in the Giants' backfield, Tracy Jr. should be off the radar of fantasy managers.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. (illness) off injury report for Week 2
metadata.description: Tyrone Tracy Jr. (illness) is off of the injury report and will be good to go for Week 2's matchup against the Los Angeles Rams.
metadata.analysis: It was reported earlier in the week that Tracy is dealing with a serious case of the flu, but he seems to have gotten over it already, as he is no longer listed on the team's injury report and was a full go at practice on Thursday. He should continue to play his usual depth role in New York's backfield on Monday, though he doesn't carry any fantasy value at this point in the season.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. Facing an Uphill Battle for Playing Time
metadata.description: New York Giants running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. had a disastrous showing in his team's Week 1 win over the Dallas Cowboys. Tracy Jr. recorded just two carries and lost a fumble in the second quarter, which led to him being benched for the remainder of the game. While Tracy Jr. topped 1,000 scrimmage yards in both 2024 and 2025, he has a new coaching staff in 2026 and now appears to be behind both Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary on the Giants' running back depth chart. Once fellow Giants back Najee Harris is fully up to speed with the team, Tracy Jr. may fall to the RB4 spot and could even be a candidate to be released. At this point, a change of scenery would almost certainly be the best thing for Tracy Jr.'s fantasy value. Barring a trade, his release, or at least one injury in the Giants' backfield, Tracy Jr. should remain off the radar of fantasy managers in redraft leagues.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy - Comes down with illness
metadata.description: Coach John Harbaugh said Wednesday that Tracy is dealing with an illness, Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Three days removed from logging just two offensive snaps in the Giants' season-opening win against the Cowboys, Tracy wasn't able to take part in Wednesday's unofficial practice. Harbaugh believes Tracy will be back on the practice field Thursday, after which the team will post its first Week 2 injury report ahead of Monday's game at the Rams.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. (illness) absent from practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Tyrone Tracy Jr. (illness) is absent from New York's practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Tracy is reportedly dealing with a case of the flu and is not present for New York's practice on Wednesday. It sounds like this is something that could affect his availability for Sunday's game, and if he is limited or sidelined because of it, Devin Singletary would be primed for more work in his absence.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy - Two offensive snaps in Week 1
metadata.description: Tracy recorded two carries for 14 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday night's 28-20 win over Dallas.
metadata.analysis: Tracy put the ball on the ground on his second rushing attempt of the night, and Cowboys defensive lineman Quinnen Williams recovered the fumble. The running back didn't play another snap on offense the rest of the night. In total, Tracy logged two snaps on offense and nine snaps with the special-teams unit, and he'll enter Week 2 as the team's No. 3 option in the backfield behind Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary.

metadata.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. loses fumble in win Sunday
metadata.description: Tyrone Tracy Jr. rushed the ball two times for 14 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
metadata.analysis: This year's preseason saw a lot of mistakes for Tracy, and that continued on Sunday night, when he lost a fumble despite seeing just two touches over the course of the night. He is clearly the RB3 behind Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary right now and will likely remain irrelevant moving forward.
